\mxunit{enrichment-bisection-problems}{Bracketing a root by bisection}
\mxsubtitle{Upper high school · analysis and algorithms \textperiodcentered{} Synthesis problem \textperiodcentered{} 12}

\begin{problem}[Investigate, justify, conclude]
For $f(x)=x^{3}-x-1$ on $[1 ; 2]$, prove existence and uniqueness of a root $\alpha $. Carry out three bisection steps. How many halvings guarantee that the final midpoint approximates $\alpha $ with error at most $0.001$?
\end{problem}
